title: Good-$Γ$ Numbers: A Shell-Optimized Route to the Thermodynamic Limit in Quantum Monte Carlo Calculations of the High-Density Two-Dimensional Electron Gas
authors: S. Azadi, T. D. Kühne, A. Principi, M. S. Bahramy
abstract: Single-particle finite-size errors remain a central obstacle in quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations of periodic systems, conventionally reduced via twist averaging (TA). Here we introduce Good-$Γ$ (GG) particle numbers as system sizes $N$ at which the $Γ$-point Hartree--Fock (HF) energy of the high-density two-dimensional uniform electron gas (2D UEG) lies anomalously close to its thermodynamic-limit (TL) value. All results in this work concern the 2D UEG in its high-density Fermi-liquid regime, $r_s=1$--$4$. We systematically investigate the kinetic- and exchange-energy errors, $ΔKE(N)$ and $ΔEX(N)$, that underlie this one-body finite-size-error cancellation across four densities and both spin polarizations. We then compare diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC) energies extrapolated to the TL from GG-$N$ sequences against twist-averaged extrapolations at the same densities and polarizations, finding agreement to within a fraction of a millihartree in every case, independent of whether a $1/N$ or an $N^{-5/4}$ extrapolation form is used.
summary: This work introduces 'Good-$\Gamma$' numbers as a shell-optimized technique to mitigate finite-size errors in Quantum Monte Carlo simulations of the 2D electron gas. By identifying specific system sizes where one-body errors cancel out, the authors demonstrate that the resulting extrapolated energies agree remarkably well with standard twist-averaging techniques. This provides a powerful, computationally efficient diagnostic tool for achieving the thermodynamic limit in strongly correlated electron systems.
main_problem: The central challenge is reducing single-particle finite-size errors in Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations of periodic systems to accurately approach the thermodynamic limit (TL).
main_result: The Good-$\Gamma$ (GG) particle number sequence provides a robust, complementary method to Twist Averaging (TA) for extrapolating DMC energies to the TL, showing excellent agreement with established methods.
method: The authors analyze finite-size errors ($\Delta KE, \Delta EX$) by identifying specific particle numbers ($N$) where the Hartree-Fock energy is anomalously close to the TL value, allowing for systematic extrapolation.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the high-density Two-Dimensional Electron Gas (2D UEG) operating in the high-density Fermi-liquid regime ($r_s=1$ to $4$).
key_observables: Finite-size errors ($\Delta KE(N)$ and $\Delta EX(N)$), the extrapolated DMC energy to the TL ($E(\infty)$), and the ratio $\Delta EX(N)/\Delta KE(N)$.
important_parameters: Density parameter $r_s$ (1–4), system size $N$, and extrapolation forms ($1/N$ or $N^{-5/4}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is strictly limited to the high-density 2D UEG; applicability to other regimes or dimensions is not claimed.
figures_summary: Figures compare $\Delta E_{HF}(N)$ vs $1/N$ for GG vs. TA, showing the cancellation mechanism. Other figures illustrate the linear extrapolation of DMC energies to $1/N=0$ using both GG and TAV sequences.
paper_structure: The paper systematically introduces the problem of finite-size errors, defines the GG criterion based on HF energy minimization, analyzes the cancellation mechanism between kinetic and exchange energy errors, and finally compares the resulting DMC extrapolations from GG versus TA methods.
why_interesting: While focused on electron gas theory, the rigorous methodology for error control and extrapolation in strongly correlated systems is highly relevant to developing reliable numerical techniques for complex quantum materials.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

Finite-cell HF energy error, ∆EHF = EHF N −EHF ∞ (Ha/electron), as a function of 1/N for the unpolarized (ζ = 0) 2D UEG at rs = 1, 2, 3, 4, using hexagonal simulation cells, N = 102–5000. Γ-point (left column) and TA (right column) results are shown separately, one row per density. The Γ-point results oscillate in sign; the TA results remain single-signed throughout.
FIG. 2. As Fig. 1, for the fully spin-polarized (ζ = 1) 2D UEG.
